biological.citation: Inhibition of K63 ubiquitination by G-Protein pathway suppressor 2 (GPS2) regulates mitochondria-associated translation (PMID: 39094987)
biological.summary: GPS2 inhibits non-proteolytic K63 ubiquitination mediated by Ubc13 E2 enzyme. GPS2 regulates translation of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial proteins by controlling ubiquitination of RNA-binding proteins (PABPC1) and translation factors (RPS1, RACK1, eIF3M) on the outer mitochondrial membrane. Genetic deletion or stress-induced nuclear translocation of GPS2 promotes import-coupled translation and antioxidant gene expression.
biological.sample_size: mouse embryonic fibroblasts and human breast cancer cells

biological.citation: Inherited Thrombocytopenia Related Genes: GPS2 Mediates the Interplay Between ANKRD26 and ETV6 (PMID: 39791724)
biological.summary: GPS2 is a component of the NCoR complex that binds both ANKRD26 and ETV6 proteins, mediating their interaction. ANKRD26 overexpression deregulates ETV6 transcriptional repression through GPS2-mediated protein-protein interactions, revealing a novel ANKRD26-ETV6-GPS2 axis in thrombocytopenia pathogenesis.

biological.citation: G protein pathway suppressor 2 suppresses aerobic glycolysis through RACK1-mediated HIF-1α degradation in breast cancer (PMID: 38942092)
biological.summary: GPS2 is low-expressed in breast cancer tissues and negatively correlated with poor prognosis. GPS2 destabilizes HIF-1α through direct binding to RACK1, promoting HIF-1α polyubiquitination and degradation, which suppresses transcription of glycolytic regulators (PGK1, PGAM1, ENO1, PKM2, LDHA, PDK1/2/4). A GPS2-derived peptide (amino acids 70-92) promotes RACK1-HIF-1α interaction and suppresses BC tumorigenesis in vitro and in vivo.
biological.sample_size: breast cancer cell lines and in vivo xenograft models

biological.citation: GPS2 confers l-asparaginase resistance in acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through ATF4/ASNS axis (PMID: 40693356)
biological.summary: GPS2 binds to and stabilizes ATF4 protein by inhibiting its ubiquitin-proteasome degradation through impairing the interaction between ATF4 and BTRC E3 ligase. GPS2-mediated ATF4 stabilization increases ASNS expression, conferring l-asparaginase resistance in ALL cells. GPS2 knockdown sensitizes ALL cells to l-ASP treatment in vitro and increases l-ASP efficacy in vivo.
biological.sample_size: ALL cell lines and xenografted ALL tumors

biological.citation: GPS2 regulates embryonic angiogenesis by enhancing endothelial cell survival through stabilizing HOIP (PMID: 41507360)
biological.summary: GPS2 binds to the NZF domain of HOIP (catalytic subunit of LUBAC) and inhibits K48-linked polyubiquitination at K579, K737, and K988 residues, preventing HOIP proteasomal degradation. EC-specific GPS2 knockout mice are embryonic lethal at E16.5 due to defective vascularization and aberrant TNFR1-mediated endothelial cell death. GPS2 maintains LUBAC stability and activity to attenuate TNF-induced cell death.

biological.citation: ANKRD26 and its interacting partners TRIO, GPS2, HMMR and DIPA regulate adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 cells (PMID: 22666460)
biological.summary: GPS2 was identified as an ANKRD26-interacting partner by yeast two-hybrid and immunoprecipitation assays. Selective down-regulation of GPS2 increases adipogenesis in 3T3-L1 cells. GPS2, normally nuclear-localized, translocates to the cytoplasm when ANKRD26 C-terminus is introduced, indicating functional protein-protein interaction in adipogenesis regulation.

biological.citation: Liquid-liquid phase separation of GPS2-LATS1 promotes colorectal cancer progression by reprogramming lipid metabolism (PMID: 40715488)
biological.summary: GPS2 is overexpressed in colorectal cancer and promotes lipid metabolic reprogramming through dual regulation: facilitating SREBP1 nuclear translocation to activate lipid synthesis and increasing PPARα transcription to promote fatty acid oxidation. GPS2 undergoes liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) to form biomolecular condensates that interact with LATS1 kinase domain, suppressing LATS1 activity and releasing YAP to amplify lipid metabolism. GPS2 depletion inhibits tumor growth in vitro and in vivo.
biological.sample_size: CRC cell lines and in vivo tumor models

biological.citation: Nonproteolytic ubiquitination regulates chromatin occupancy by the NCoR/SMRT/HDAC3 corepressor complex in MCF-7 breast cancer cells (PMID: 40305047)
biological.summary: Nuclear GPS2 is required for licensing HDAC3 recruitment to chromatin via restricted ubiquitination by TRAF6 E3 ligase. GPS2 regulates the switch from repressive to activating functions of the NCoR/SMRT complex. TRAF6-mediated ubiquitination of TAB2 (facultative NCoR/SMRT component) contributes to corepressor clearance from target regulatory regions in response to IL-1β stimulation.
biological.sample_size: MCF-7 breast cancer cells with genome-wide RNA-seq and ChIP-seq

biological.citation: GPS2-mediated regulation of the adipocyte secretome modulates adipose tissue remodeling at the onset of diet-induced obesity (PMID: 36731652)
biological.summary: Adipocyte-specific GPS2 knockout (GPS2-AKO) mice show impaired adaptation to high-fat diet, with increased inflammation, insulin resistance, and obesity compared to wildtype. Loss of GPS2 in adipocytes alters stromal cell populations and increases expression of secreted factors promoting TGFβ-driven fibrotic microenvironment. GPS2 regulates transcriptional rewiring of adipocyte-derived exosomal cargo critical for healthy tissue remodeling.
biological.sample_size: adipocyte-specific GPS2-KO mice with single-cell RNA-seq and proteomics

biological.citation: ASHG 2010 - A functional analysis of GABARAP on 17p13.1 by knockdown zebrafish (T. Yamamoto et al.)
biological.summary: GPS2 is located in the 17p13.1 microdeletion region associated with mental retardation, intractable epilepsy, and dysmorphic features. GPS2 is noted as having functional importance in neuronal development alongside DLG4/PSD95 and GABARAP. No pathogenic mutations in GPS2 were found in a cohort of 142 patients with idiopathic developmental delay with/without epilepsy.
